quotes.quote: And so the dirty secret of forward deployed engineering, I won't make you wait until the end, is it doesn't exist. It is a term that it is meant to describe so many things that it sort of means nothing at this point.
But nonetheless, it's sort of the hottest job in AI. And so what I hope to convince you of over the next, let's say, 15 minutes is A that this is true and B that this doesn't matter.
These days you lead with, you know, you speak a certain language, you have these skill sets. They were leading with location.
But in practice, forward-deployed engineering actually started as something more akin to DevOps. And so, platform stability really constituted the bulk of the job early on.
In fact, my onboarding project at Palantir was actually deploy the software on an EC2 instance. And so, that was literally the job.
I like to think of data integration software without integrated data as a movie theater that's playing nothing. It's like, why show up, you know?
So, so basically, forward deployed engineers now have this dual role, right? DevOps plus data integration.
One of the things they found, a spoiler alert for anyone building a dashboarding platform, is that a dashboard that doesn't write back to the data source isn't that useful.
And they also need a solution that doesn't involve shipping people out to Finland or Canberra or choose the kind of location on the earlier slide of your preference.
So, what's interesting about this is these weren't discrete eras, right? The total FTE jobs to be done actually increased over time.

It's actually the best training ground for generalists. And in fact, this is why I would say that Palantir has seen such success Palantir alums founding companies is because it's actually training you on all of these different facets of the role.
Which is what vintage of FDE are you?
You know, I don't know how many of you have been a staff eng for eight years with six years of direct sales experience and four years as a solution architect.
And so you think about the the dirty secret that it doesn't exist and actually it it either doesn't exist or maybe it actually exists too much.
the one continuity point is that you actually have every single forward deployed engineer accountable to the customer

But I think something more interesting is happening that we're seeing at Sierra, which is actually the lines are blurring. So product engineering is also becoming more client-facing.

if you have both of these things, you have forward-deployed engineers that can now contribute to the product, you have more outcome-based pricing, how do you actually guarantee the outcome? And that really is forward-deployed engineering.

really in some ways everything is forward deployed engineering, or at least everything is trending that way. Product engineering, agent engineering, AI engineering, solutions engineering, and customer engineering.
forward deployed engineering is dead. And long live forward deployed engineering.

positions.claim: The term 'forward deployed engineer' has no coherent definition because it has been used to describe too many different jobs.
Forward deployed engineering began as DevOps work, not as customer-facing solutioning; platform stability was the bulk of the early job.
The 'forward deployed' label originally referred to physical location because Palantir's deployments were largely on-prem.
Data integration software is not useful without someone doing the integration work, which is what made FDEs commercially necessary.
A dashboard that doesn't write back to its data source decays in usefulness over time.
The FDE eras were not discrete; the total jobs-to-be-done accumulated, making the role the best training ground for generalists.
Palantir alumni's success at founding companies is caused by the FDE role training them across many facets of building and selling software.
Hiring managers should ask candidates what 'vintage' of FDE they are rather than treating the title as a single skill set.
Because coding agents make code cheap, FDEs can now ship end-to-end solutions rather than only prototypes, making them more impactful in product development.
Product engineering and forward deployed engineering are converging: product engineers are becoming more client-facing while FDEs contribute to product.
Most software pricing in this market will move to outcome-based pricing, with usage-based pricing (e.g. foundation model APIs) as an intermediate point.
Guaranteeing customer outcomes is the essential function of forward deployed engineering, which is what makes outcome-based pricing viable.
Agent engineering is a subset or flavor of forward deployed engineering focused on outcomes, rather than a fully separate discipline as the speaker argued in 2024.
All engineering disciplines that touch customers are trending toward forward deployed engineering.
